stories.sourceTitle: FDA Approves First Plasmid DNA-based Immunotherapy for Adults with Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis
supportingPassages: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval for Voceryq (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd) for treatment of adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), a rare disease caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) that leads to the formation of small, wart-like growths in the patient’s airways.

This approval, the first for a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy in the U.S., offers patients a new therapeutic option that targets the root cause of RRP and has been shown to reduce the burden of surgical intervention, representing an important step forward for a patient population with limited treatment options.

The agency based this accelerated approval on clinical trial data showing Voceryq helps reduce the frequency of surgical procedures required to remove growths in adult patients with RRP — an intermediate clinical endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.
Personal income increased $54.5 billion (0.2 percent at a monthly rate) in September, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA).
Disposable personal income (DPI)—personal income less personal current taxes—increased $52.7 billion (0.2 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $113.1 billion (0.5 percent).
From the preceding month, the PCE price index for September increased 0.5 percent.

stories.sourceTitle: FTC, Washington Take Action Against Payment Processor for Deceiving Small Businesses About Costs and Cancellation Terms
supportingPassages: Small businesses also will be able to rescind processing agreements without a termination penalty under the proposed order settling the FTC and Washington’s allegations.

The FTC and Washington allege that Riverside’s sales pitches included a quote sheet that compared the costs prospective clients paid their existing payment processor with the amount they would save if they used Riverside’s services instead.
The FTC alleges that Riverside’s practices violated the FTC Act and the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act by obtaining consumers’ financial information by using false or fraudulent statements.
